channel.title: Tom Pickup
channel.description: News and updates from Tom Pickup.

item.title: Nine Front Doors: Supported Living Starts in Lytham St Annes
item.description: Work has started on nine supported living apartments in Lytham St Annes for people with a learning disability and autistic people. Completion summer 2027.
item.author: Tom Pickup

item.title: The state cannot see its own data centres
item.description: The ONS says data centres are not separately visible in the national accounts. The grid operator's connection queue is fourteen times its own forecast.
item.author: Tom Pickup

item.title: Two Wind Farms, One View, and No Assessment of Either Together
item.description: Fifty-one turbines are proposed on the South Pennine moors, 15.7 kilometres apart. Neither applicant has assessed the combined view. So I mapped it.
item.author: Tom Pickup

item.title: The LCCA's data observatory is 'a concept'. So we built one over the weekend.
item.description: Officers admitted the promised data observatory did not exist. By Monday we had one live: 104,161 Lancashire companies, nine tools, built at no cost to you.
item.author: Tom Pickup

item.title: Four Councils, One Decision: I Modelled What Lancashire's Reorganisation Actually Means
item.description: 15 councils become 4 from April 2028. An interactive, sourced model of the new councils, their budgets, the need they inherit and what it will cost.
item.author: Tom Pickup

item.title: The Asylum System Is Dumping Its Bill on Burnley
item.description: I went through every penny Burnley Council spends on temporary accommodation. In one year the asylum share of its homelessness went from 1 in 60 to 1 in 9.
item.author: Tom Pickup

item.title: Where Burnley Council's Money Goes: Every Payment Over £500 in 2025/26
item.description: Burnley Borough Council spent £38.06 million in payments of £500 or more last year, across 4,489 transactions to 843 suppliers. Every line, searchable.
item.author: Tom Pickup

item.title: Nine in Ten Crimes in Lancashire End With No One Charged
item.description: Report a crime in Lancashire and the odds anyone is charged are about one in ten. That is one of the better records in the country. The real numbers.
item.author: Tom Pickup

item.title: Lancashire's Crime Divide: Four Times the Crime in One County
item.description: I ranked all fourteen Lancashire districts by crime rate. A four to one gap that tracks deprivation. Not a high-crime county, a divided one.
item.author: Tom Pickup

item.title: Put the Police Back on Burnley's Streets
item.description: Violent crime in Burnley runs about a third above the national average, yet the neighbourhood officers who prevent it have been cut by more than half.
item.author: Tom Pickup

item.title: What the Councils Own in Burnley: Every Public Title, Mapped
item.description: Burnley Borough Council and Lancashire County Council hold more than a thousand property titles in the town. Every one I could place, on a map.
item.author: Tom Pickup

item.title: They Want to Work. The System Will Not Let Them.
item.description: Most disabled people out of work want a job. A frozen savings limit, a year-long support backlog and a shortage of accessible vehicles stop them.
item.author: Tom Pickup

item.title: Sick Sooner, Out of Work, Gone Earlier: The Burnley Trap
item.description: Burnley is the 4th most deprived town in England. Its people fall ill younger, are pushed out of work by that illness, and die sooner than almost anywhere.
item.author: Tom Pickup

item.title: PIP Fraud Quadrupled to £410 Million. The Real Leak Is £5.4 Billion.
item.description: Fraud in the disability benefit PIP quadrupled in a year. The same figures show £6.8 billion lost to benefit fraud overall, most of it nowhere near PIP.
item.author: Tom Pickup

item.title: Nearly One in Five New Cars in Britain Now Runs on Benefits
item.description: Motability puts nearly one in five new cars on Britain's roads, holds £3.9 billion in reserves and pays its boss £924,000. What it costs, and who qualifies.
item.author: Tom Pickup

item.title: Where Your Rent Goes in Burnley
item.description: Rents in Burnley are rising, most renters now pay a private landlord, and a large slice of it is public money. Meanwhile the help with rent is frozen.
item.author: Tom Pickup

item.title: 638 Empty Homes, 2,657 Families Waiting
item.description: Burnley has hundreds of homes standing empty long term while thousands of families wait for somewhere to live. The two numbers, side by side.
item.author: Tom Pickup

item.title: Ten Thousand People in Burnley Are on PIP. This Is the Bill for Managed Decline.
item.description: More than ten thousand people in Burnley claim the disability benefit PIP, the 47th highest of 543 seats in England. This is why.
item.author: Tom Pickup

item.title: The Shared Houses Burnley Cannot See
item.description: The official statistics say Burnley has 65 shared houses. The council's own research says 916, and it had no record of more than half of them.
item.author: Tom Pickup

item.title: Who Owns Burnley? Increasingly, Not the People Who Live Here
item.description: Ten years of public records for my home town. More of Burnley is bought up by landlords, companies and faraway funds while local families are priced out.
item.author: Tom Pickup

item.title: The Names Behind the Doors: Burnley's Biggest Property Owners
item.description: I pulled HM Land Registry's record of every company that owns property in Burnley. The biggest owner is a faraway fund, not a local landlord.
item.author: Tom Pickup

item.title: More People, Fewer Homes: The Squeeze Nobody in Burnley Voted For
item.description: In ten years Burnley's population grew almost entirely through immigration, home ownership fell, and the cheap housing was bought up to rent out.
item.author: Tom Pickup
